tasteReview.beats: No win named — the page shows no populated or sample state, so it cannot be judged as beating Zillow's, Redfin's, or Realtor.com's own compare-tool onboarding, which at minimum surface a populated tray or recently-viewed thumbnails.
tasteReview.dullest: The entire visible content block ('Up to four homes' plus its three links) — it is the only section on the page besides chrome, and it is text and arrows with nothing to look at.
tasteReview.verdict: This still reads as a placeholder that grew better breadcrumbs, not a finished page. Turning one text link into three quick links answered the letter of the last critique without touching the substance: there is still nothing on screen that shows a visitor what a finished four-home comparison looks like, and still zero interaction in the first viewport. Ship the sample-populated state, or don't ship this screen as the page's front door.

defects.finding: No illustration of the populated comparison exists anywhere in the first viewport on either shot — no sample rows, thumbnails, or feature-table preview — so a visitor cannot see what a finished four-home comparison looks like before committing effort to adding homes.
defects.primitive: likely the V3Quiet-based empty-state block for the /compare route
defects.fix: Add a static mock of the populated table (2-4 photo thumbnails + a few feature rows: price, beds, baths) beneath the paragraph so the page demonstrates its own job.

defects.section: quick-link row (Search homes for sale / Every city / Price drops)
defects.finding: The three rows are plain navigation links with a trailing arrow to other pages; none is a data section, so the first viewport contains zero in-page interaction that rewards a hover, tap, scrub or toggle with more data.
defects.primitive: link-row list component under the 'Up to four homes' heading
defects.fix: Replace at least one link with an inline interactive element, e.g. a hoverable sample comparison card that reveals feature columns on hover instead of navigating away.

defects.section: descriptive paragraph under 'Up to four homes'
defects.finding: The body copy ('Add homes from any search or listing page...') renders in a light gray whose luminance sits close to the #faf8f4 ground, a likely AA contrast shortfall at this text size.
defects.fix: Darken the paragraph color (or raise weight) to clear 4.5:1 contrast against cream.

defects.finding: Nothing in the page's own content (as opposed to inherited nav, footer, and H1) is specific to home-comparison or Central Oregon — heading, one paragraph, three generic links is a shape any empty-list utility screen would use for any product.
defects.fix: Give the section a visual anchor unique to comparing homes, e.g. a stacked/fanned photo motif standing in for the four open slots.
